source.mediumDifference: Tamil Q5 explicitly requests Cramer's rule; English Q5 does not repeat that instruction. Both give identical meal data and budget. Preserve each medium's wording.

models.q: Solve the following systems of linear equations by Cramer’s rule: (i) 5x − 2y + 16 = 0, x + 3y − 7 = 0

modelling.en: Move the constants to the right-hand sides, preserving their signs.

models.q: Solve the following systems of linear equations by Cramer’s rule: (ii) 3/x + 2y = 12, 2/x + 3y = 13

modelling.en: After the reciprocal substitution, the two equations are linear in u_x and y.

models.q: Solve the following systems of linear equations by Cramer’s rule: (iii) 3x + 3y − z = 11, 2x − y + 2z = 9, 4x + 3y + 2z = 25
Solve the following systems of linear equations by Cramer’s rule: (iv) 3/x − 4/y − 2/z − 1 = 0, 1/x + 2/y + 1/z − 2 = 0, 2/x − 5/y − 4/z + 1 = 0

modelling.en: Move the constant terms to the right and use the three reciprocal variables. In the first equation the coefficient of 1/z is negative.

models.q: In a competitive examination, one mark is awarded for every correct answer while 1/4 mark is deducted for every wrong answer. A student answered 100 questions and got 80 marks. How many questions did he answer correctly ? (Use Cramer’s rule to solve the problem).

modelling.en: Let c be the number of correct answers and w the number of wrong answers. Both are nonnegative integers. Every answered question is either correct or wrong.
Each correct answer earns one mark and each wrong answer loses one quarter of a mark.

models.q: A chemist has one solution which is 50% acid and another solution which is 25% acid. How much each should be mixed to make 10 litres of a 40% acid solution ? (Use Cramer’s rule to solve the problem).

modelling.en: Let h and l be the litres of the 50% and 25% solutions respectively. Their volumes add to 10 litres.
The final mixture contains 40% of 10 litres, or 4 litres, of pure acid. Balance the acid amounts using exact fractions.

models.answer: Mix 6 litres of the 50% solution and 4 litres of the 25% solution.

models.q: A fish tank can be filled in 10 minutes using both pumps A and B simultaneously. However, pump B can pump water in or out at the same rate. If pump B is inadvertently run in reverse, then the tank will be filled in 30 minutes. How long would it take each pump to fill the tank by itself ? (Use Cramer’s rule to solve the problem).

modelling.en: Let a and b be the times in minutes for pumps A and B to fill one tank individually. Their filling rates are u_a = 1/a and u_b = 1/b tanks per minute, both positive.
Running pump B in reverse subtracts its rate. The remaining net rate fills one tank in 30 minutes.

models.answer: Pump A: 15 minutes; pump B: 30 minutes.

models.q: A family of 3 people went out for dinner in a restaurant. The cost of two dosai, three idlies and two vadais is ₹ 150. The cost of the two dosai, two idlies and four vadais is ₹ 200. The cost of five dosai, four idlies and two vadais is ₹ 250. The family has ₹ 350 in hand and they ate 3 dosai and six idlies and six vadais. Will they be able to manage to pay the bill within the amount they had ?

modelling.en: Let d, i and v be the prices in rupees of one dosai, one idli and one vadai. Translate each of the three quoted meals into an equation in the same order.

afterSolution.en: The family ordered three dosai, six idlies and six vadais. Add those item costs and compare the bill with ₹350.

models.answer: Yes. Bill = ₹330; balance = ₹20. One dosai = ₹30, one idli = ₹10, one vadai = ₹30.
